items.label: f03-two-terms
items.back: MeetingTerm: end must be strictly after start (equal rejects), checked in the factory. Term: nullable bounds, no order check at construction, IsInTerm inclusive at both ends; a missing bound is unbounded.

items.label: f01-occupied-places
items.front: Meeting capacity: what counts as an occupied place?
items.back: Sum over attendees where IsActive (no decision change, not removed) of 1 + guests. The host is an attendee and takes a place. Record count, identities and places are different numbers.

items.label: f02-addattendee-order
items.back: before start -> inside RSVP -> group member -> not a duplicate (IsActiveAttendee) -> guest limit (only when > 0) -> total places (only when not null; equal allowed) -> change an active not-attendee decision -> append the attendee.

items.label: f04-mutate-then-throw
items.back: Demoting an ordinary attendee: the child already-attendee rule throws before any change. Demoting the last host: the child changes role and appends its event, then the aggregate host-count rule throws. A thrown exception does not prove unchanged state.

items.prompt: Ben is the only active waitlist member. Cara, who was never an attendee, calls AddNotAttendee. What happens to Ben?

choices.text: Ben is promoted with the guest count he signed up with
Nothing, since no attendee changed a decision to free a place
Ben is promoted anyway; promotion does not need a freed seat
Ben is promoted only if total capacity allows another place

choices: Ben is promoted with the guest count he signed up with
Nothing, since no attendee changed a decision to free a place
Ben is promoted anyway; promotion does not need a freed seat
Ben is promoted only if total capacity allows another place

items.explanation: After adding the not-attendee record, the method calls attendee?.ChangeDecision() (a no-op for Cara) and then unconditionally promotes the first active waitlist member. No capacity or AddAttendee guards run for him, and he gets 0 guests.

items.prompt: Before the start, Cancel is called by member A and then again by member B. What does the second call do?

choices.text: It throws, since a meeting cannot be cancelled a second time
It replaces the cancel member with B, then adds a second event
Nothing visible: no new event, and A stays the cancelling member
It adds a second event but keeps A as the cancelling member

choices: It throws, since a meeting cannot be cancelled a second time
It replaces the cancel member with B, then adds a second event
Nothing visible: no new event, and A stays the cancelling member
It adds a second event but keeps A as the cancelling member

items.explanation: Cancel checks the start rule, then mutates only if !_isCanceled. The second call skips the block: no state change and no MeetingCanceledDomainEvent. After the start, the same call would throw instead.

items.prompt: A future meeting was cancelled. An eligible group member then calls AddAttendee within the RSVP term. What happens?

choices.text: It succeeds but the attendee is created as already removed
It succeeds, as AddAttendee never checks the cancelled flag
It throws, as cancellation is a terminal state for every method
It throws MeetingCannotBeChangedAfterStartRule after cancelling

choices: It succeeds but the attendee is created as already removed
It succeeds, as AddAttendee never checks the cancelled flag
It throws, as cancellation is a terminal state for every method
It throws MeetingCannotBeChangedAfterStartRule after cancelling

items.explanation: Only Cancel reads _isCanceled. AddAttendee runs its own six rules, none of which looks at cancellation, so the member is added.

items.prompt: A meeting has an attendee limit of 5 and a guest limit above 3. Its creator is the only host. A member joins with 3 guests. Then another member asks to join with 0 guests. What happens?

choices.text: Accepted; only the two attendee records are counted
Rejected by the total-capacity rule, needing 6 places of 5
Rejected by the guest-number rule, which runs first
Accepted, since the creator host does not take up a place

choices: Accepted; only the two attendee records are counted
Rejected by the total-capacity rule, needing 6 places of 5
Rejected by the guest-number rule, which runs first
Accepted, since the creator host does not take up a place

items.explanation: Occupied places are the active attendees plus their guests: creator 1 + member 4 = 5. The new request needs 5 + 1 + 0 = 6, and 5 < 6 breaks MeetingAttendeesNumberIsAboveLimitRule. The guest rule passes for 0 guests.

items.prompt: SystemClock.Now is exactly equal to a meeting's StartDate. Does MeetingCannotBeChangedAfterStartRule block a change at that instant?

choices.text: Yes: a meeting counts as started at its StartDate
No; IsAfterStart uses a strict greater-than comparison
No, but only because SystemClock rounds down to seconds
Yes, as the rule also rejects any time within one minute

choices: Yes: a meeting counts as started at its StartDate
No; IsAfterStart uses a strict greater-than comparison
No, but only because SystemClock rounds down to seconds
Yes, as the rule also rejects any time within one minute

items.explanation: IsAfterStart returns SystemClock.Now > StartDate. At exact equality it is false, so the rule is not broken; one tick later it is.

items.prompt: The creator is the meeting's only active host and demotes themselves with SetAttendeeRole. What is the in-memory state when the call returns?

choices.text: It throws after the role and the event already changed
It throws before anything changes, so the host role is intact
It succeeds and leaves the meeting with no host at all
It throws, because an actor cannot change their own role

choices: It throws after the role and the event already changed
It throws before anything changes, so the host role is intact
It succeeds and leaves the meeting with no host at all
It throws, because an actor cannot change their own role

items.explanation: SetAsAttendee assigns the role and adds MemberSetAsAttendeeDomainEvent; only then does Meeting count active hosts (0) and check MeetingMustHaveAtLeastOneHostRule. The exception does not undo the mutation.

items.prompt: After the meeting has started, a non-member of the group asks to attend with 20 guests, far above every limit. Which rule rejects the call?

choices.text: MeetingGuestsNumberIsAboveLimitRule, as 20 guests is far too many
MeetingAttendeeMustBeAMemberOfGroupRule, as the caller is no member
MeetingAttendeesNumberIsAboveLimitRule, which runs before the rest
MeetingCannotBeChangedAfterStartRule, checked first

choices: MeetingGuestsNumberIsAboveLimitRule, as 20 guests is far too many
MeetingAttendeeMustBeAMemberOfGroupRule, as the caller is no member
MeetingAttendeesNumberIsAboveLimitRule, which runs before the rest
MeetingCannotBeChangedAfterStartRule, checked first

items.explanation: CheckRule throws on the first broken rule, and AddAttendee checks start time first, then RSVP, group membership, duplicates, guests and total capacity. The later problems are never evaluated.

items.prompt: Waitlist: Ada signs up at 09:00, Ben at 09:05, Ada signs off at 09:10, and Ada signs up again at 09:15. Who is promoted next?

choices.text: Ada, since her first sign-up at 09:00 is the earliest
Ada, as rejoining reactivates her original record
Ben, because Ada's 09:00 record is no longer active
Neither; nobody moves until someone signs off again

choices: Ada, since her first sign-up at 09:00 is the earliest
Ada, as rejoining reactivates her original record
Ben, because Ada's 09:00 record is no longer active
Neither; nobody moves until someone signs off again

items.explanation: Selection filters to IsActive() records and orders by SignUpDate. Ada's first record is signed off; her second record is 09:15; Ben's 09:05 is the earliest active one.

items.prompt: A meeting has guest limit 0 and no attendee limit (null). An eligible member asks to join with 4 guests. What does AddAttendee do?

choices.text: It rejects in MeetingLimits, as 0 guests is not a valid limit
It accepts: a guest limit of 0 turns the guest check off
It rejects, because a limit of 0 means no guests are allowed
It rejects, since a null attendee limit counts as zero places

choices: It rejects in MeetingLimits, as 0 guests is not a valid limit
It accepts: a guest limit of 0 turns the guest check off
It rejects, because a limit of 0 means no guests are allowed
It rejects, since a null attendee limit counts as zero places

items.explanation: MeetingGuestsNumberIsAboveLimitRule is broken only when guestsLimit > 0 and guestsLimit < requested, so 0 disables it; a null attendee limit disables the total rule. Nothing rejects the request.

items.prompt: Ben joined the waitlist when the event fee was 10. The fee is now 15 when AddNotAttendee promotes him. Which fee is stored on his new attendee record?

choices.text: No fee: promoted members are created with MoneyValue.Undefined
The fee of 10, as captured on his waitlist record at sign-up
Twice the current fee, as the waitlist adds a guest place
The current fee of 15, read from the meeting at promotion time

choices: No fee: promoted members are created with MoneyValue.Undefined
The fee of 10, as captured on his waitlist record at sign-up
Twice the current fee, as the waitlist adds a guest place
The current fee of 15, read from the meeting at promotion time

items.explanation: Promotion calls MeetingAttendee.CreateNew with zero guests and this._eventFee, the meeting's current fee. The waitlist member has no fee field, and (1 + 0) * fee is just the fee.

It succeeds, and the guest limit is clamped down to 4
It throws only once a meeting already holds 5 people

items.prompt: An attendee was removed with RemoveAttendee (their decision never changed). Before the start, inside RSVP, they ask to join again. What does the current code do?

choices.text: Rejects it as a duplicate, since IsActiveAttendee ignores removal
Rejected: removal also takes them out of the group
Accepts it, because the removed record no longer counts as active
Accepts it and reactivates the original attendee record

choices: Rejects it as a duplicate, since IsActiveAttendee ignores removal
Rejected: removal also takes them out of the group
Accepts it, because the removed record no longer counts as active
Accepts it and reactivates the original attendee record

items.explanation: The duplicate rule looks up records with IsActiveAttendee, which checks identity and !_decisionChanged only. Remove sets _isRemoved, not _decisionChanged, so the old record still matches. Capacity, by contrast, uses IsActive and does exclude it.
